function: SAC deep RL agent jointly sets IRS phase shifts, NOMA power allocation and power-splitting factors to maximize secrecy sum-rate under packet-loss and energy-harvesting constraints (p. 9).
system: RU with directional antennas, scalar transmit signal; two IoT devices and one eavesdropper (single-antenna channels); semi-passive reflecting IRS, M=64; indoor; frequency band not stated (p. 3, p. 10).
method: Soft Actor-Critic v2 deep reinforcement learning (twin critics, automatic entropy tuning), two 256-unit hidden layers; trained online by interaction with the simulated environment (p. 9, p. 10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: cascaded Rician fading (K=10), path-loss exponent 2.2, fixed distances, Gilbert-Elliott packet-loss model; no dataset or measurements; 1,000 Monte Carlo runs (p. 10).
test_conditions: Agent trained 1.6e5 steps in simulator; swept distances, eavesdropper position, SIC imperfection, M to 256, users to 10; no distinct test conditions stated (p. 17).
baselines: Exhaustive grid-based search (GBS) only; fixed power allocation shown as conventional baseline (p. 11); no learned baseline compared (p. 13).
metrics: Secure sum-rate (bit/s/Hz), harvested energy, packet-loss probability, reward convergence, FLOP-based complexity versus GBS (p. 11, p. 15).
complexity: FLOP-based complexity formulas for SAC learning and inference (Eqs. 43-47) versus exponential GBS (Eq. 48); SAC uses 10.06% of GBS resources at M=64 (p. 8, p. 15).
q1_support: p. 10: "are modeled as Rician with factor K1 = K2 = 10"
q2_support: p. 17: "evaluated as a function of the number of IRS reflecting elements M (up to 256)"
q3_support: p. 13: "We use GBS as a benchmark for the SecureO-RAN-SAC performance"
q4_support: p. 8: "the FLOPs of the actor and the twin critics"
q5_support: p. 10: "are modeled as Rician with factor K1 = K2 = 10"
notes: Included, area 3: the SAC agent outputs the IRS phase-shift matrix with NOMA power allocation and power splitting (p. 9, action vector). Packet loss is only an analytical constraint derived from SINR (p. 5), so the learned decision is physical layer. q1=0: custom cascaded Rician simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data (p. 10). q2=0: the paper never states that an agent trained in one setting is tested in another; it sweeps M, users, K and distances (pp. 15-17), and the action includes Phi_M (p. 9). q3=0: only the non-learned GBS benchmark (p. 13); no earlier learned method or standard DRL baseline (no DDPG, DQN or TD3 anywhere); the fixed alpha=0.2 curves of Figs. 4-8 are not compared with the learned method. q4=1: FLOP-based complexity of SAC training and inference, Eqs. 43-47 on p. 8, and 10.06% of GBS cost at M=64 on p. 15. q5=0: no code or data release; the only link is ref. [36], the first author's PhD dissertation (p. 18), not stated to hold code or data.
